description.text: Federico Hermanin de Reichenfeld was born in Rome to a Protestant family of Austro‑German origin. He studied philology at the University of Rome, graduating in 1895, and then turned to art history under the guidance of Adolfo Venturi, winning a scholarship to catalogue the national print collection at the Galleria nazionale d'arte antica.

From 1898 to 1938 Hermanin directed the Galleria nazionale d'arte antica and the Gabinetto nazionale delle stampe, expanded their collections, and published a series of catalogues and monographs. He also served as superintendent of the Lazio and Abruzzi galleries, oversaw restorations of major works, and founded the art journal *Roma* in 1923, which later became the official voice of the Istituto nazionale di studi romani.

curiosities.text: During restorations at Santa Cecilia in Trastevere in 1900, Hermanin uncovered a 14th‑century fresco of the Judgment, which he attributed to the Roman painter Pietro Cavallini.
